title: Borrowed from the brain
sub: The second film of What an agent is, a series on what an AI agent is and what it isn't: why brains began with moving, and why the first learning machine was modelled on a nerve cell; how nerve cells carry messages and learn, in a jellyfish, a bee, an octopus and us; a brain that guesses a step ahead and learns from its prediction errors; what models borrowed from brains and what they didn't; why a model's answer changes, and fills a missing fact with a likely one; and an agent that, like a brain, says what it expects of the data and checks.
howto: The film is drawn in the module's look: a pale marble wall over an oak floor, light from a window on the right, and nature painted full-frame, matte and soft-lit. Living nerve cells are warm, the colour of ink and lamplight; the units people built on them are violet, the model's colour. A signal on its way is a spark of warm light; orange is data and where it came from, green what is checked, amber a guess. Each scene from the past has its place and year on a tag.
